title: Continuous-function abelian sheaves on profinite sets
statement: Work on the coherent site of profinite sets in a fixed universe, with covers the finite jointly surjective families [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]; take abelian groups in a universe large enough for all continuous-map groups. Let $G$ be an abelian group with a topology for which addition and negation are continuous, without any separation assumption. Set $P_G(S)=C(S,G)$, with pointwise abelian group operations and restriction $h\mapsto h\circ u$ along a continuous map $u:T\to S$. Then $P_G$ is an abelian sheaf. Explicitly, every compatible family $h_i:S_i\to G$ on a finite jointly surjective profinite cover has a unique continuous glued section $h:S\to G$, and $P_G(\varnothing)$ is the zero group. For a continuous additive map $f:G\to H$, postcomposition $h\mapsto f\circ h$ defines a morphism $P_f:P_G\to P_H$ of abelian sheaves. These formulas define an additive functor: $P_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$, $P_{gf}=P_gP_f$ and $P_{f+g}=P_f+P_g$.

source.place: First two sentences of lem-sfb-subfield-flat.proof.md: continuous-function abelian sheaves behind the coordinate maps; extracted original steps 1 and additive part of 4.

proof.text: For $a,b\in C(S,G)$ put $(a+b)(s)=a(s)+b(s)$, $(-a)(s)=-a(s)$ and $0(s)=0$. These maps are continuous: the sum is addition composed with $s\mapsto(a(s),b(s))$, negation is negation composed with $a$, and zero is constant. Every abelian group identity holds after evaluation at each $s$, so these operations make $C(S,G)$ an abelian group. Precomposition is continuous and satisfies $(a+b)\circ u=a\circ u+b\circ u$ and $0\circ u=0$. The identities $a\circ\mathrm{id}=a$ and $(a\circ u)\circ v=a\circ(u\circ v)$ give the presheaf laws.

source.place: First paragraph: pointwise algebra and precomposition, with abelian groups replacing rings.

proof.text: For a finite family of profinite sets $S_i$, restriction gives an additive bijection $C(\coprod_i S_i,G)\longrightarrow\prod_i C(S_i,G)$. Its inverse assigns the function $a(i,s)=a_i(s)$ to a tuple $(a_i)$. For every open $O\subseteq G$, its inverse image is the union of the open subsets $a_i^{-1}(O)$ inside the open coproduct components, hence is open. Both maps preserve addition and zero by evaluation, so they are inverse group homomorphisms. Thus this is also a product in abelian groups: a family of homomorphisms $B\to C(S_i,G)$ factors uniquely through the displayed tuple map. When the family is empty there is exactly one function from the empty space to $G$, so $P_G(\varnothing)$ is the zero group.

source.place: Condition (a): continuous maps out of finite disjoint unions, including the empty union.

proof.text: Let $q:S^{\prime}\to S$ be a continuous surjection of profinite sets and put $R=S^{\prime}\times_S S^{\prime}=\{(x,y):q(x)=q(y)\}$. If $b\in C(S^{\prime},G)$ has equal pullbacks to $R$, then $b(x)=b(y)$ whenever $q(x)=q(y)$. Consequently there is a unique function $a:S\to G$ with $a\circ q=b$: define $a(s)$ to be $b(x)$ for any lift $x$ of $s$, independently of the lift by that equality. By [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient], $q$ is a quotient map, since $S^{\prime}$ is compact and $S$ is Hausdorff. For every open $O\subseteq G$, $q^{-1}(a^{-1}(O))=b^{-1}(O)$ is open; the cited open-set criterion makes $a^{-1}(O)$ open. Hence $a$ is continuous. Surjectivity of $q$ gives uniqueness among continuous sections too. Hausdorffness is required only of $S$, never of $G$.

source.place: Condition (b): descent along a compact-to-Hausdorff quotient map; Stacks Tags 08YD (lemma-closed-map) and 0AAU (lemma-closed-morphism-quotient-topology, part (3)).

proof.text: The forgetful functor from abelian groups to sets reflects finite limits. Identify the underlying type-valued presheaf of the prescribed lifted continuous-map groups with ContinuousMap.yonedaPresheaf Profinite.toTopCat G followed by uliftFunctor; the components of this natural isomorphism are identity maps. Universe lifting preserves and reflects the type-valued sheaf condition. For the unlifted presheaf, Mathlib supplies preservation of finite products and equalizerCondition_yonedaPresheaf. The latter uses [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient] for each effective epimorphism, which is surjective by Profinite.effectiveEpi_tfae. Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-coherent-sheaf-criterion] to obtain its sheaf property. Then Presheaf.isSheaf_coherent_of_hasPullbacks_of_comp reflects the finite product and equalizer limits along the forgetful functor, proving the abelian-valued sheaf condition. This replaces the hand-written test-group equalizer calculation by the existing finite-limit-reflection API, without changing the continuous sections or imposing separation on G.

source.place: Conditions (a), (b) and the coherent sheaf criterion; the abelian equalizer universal property is written explicitly.

proof.text: For the finite jointly surjective family q_i:U_i to S, use the topological sigma type of the U_i as the finite disjoint union. The maps q(i,x)=q_i(x) and b(i,x)=h_i(x) are continuous by continuous_sigma; the sigma type is compact because the indexing type is finite. Joint surjectivity makes q surjective, and [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient] makes q a quotient map since S is Hausdorff. Compatibility says precisely Function.FactorsThrough b q. The continuous map q.lift b therefore descends b; q.lift_comp gives the restriction identities. Evaluating any competing section at a lift of each s proves uniqueness. The same construction covers the empty family and empty spaces without any nonempty assumption.

source.place: Conditions (a), (b): combine the finite disjoint union and surjective descent calculations to obtain the stated gluing formula.

proof.text: For a continuous additive map $f:G\to H$, the map $P_f(S):a\mapsto f\circ a$ is defined on continuous sections by composition. It preserves addition and zero because $f(a(s)+b(s))=f(a(s))+f(b(s))$ and $f(0)=0$. It commutes with restriction since $f\circ(a\circ u)=(f\circ a)\circ u$, so it is a morphism of the constructed abelian sheaves. On each section, $P_{\mathrm{id}}(a)=a$ and $P_{gf}(a)=g\circ f\circ a=P_g(P_f(a))$. For two continuous additive maps $f,g:G\to H$, their pointwise sum is additive because $H$ is abelian and continuous because addition in $H$ is continuous. Evaluation gives $P_{f+g}(a)(s)=f(a(s))+g(a(s))=(P_f(a)+P_g(a))(s)$; also $P_0(a)=0$. Addition of sheaf morphisms is sectionwise addition of these homomorphisms, so the displayed equality is equality of sheaf morphisms. These formulas prove the asserted additive functor laws.

source.place: First paragraph (pointwise operations and functoriality), adapted to additive postcomposition; realizes the additive coordinate maps in the first two sentences of lem-sfb-subfield-flat.proof.md.
